statement: The function returns a result r and len(r) = n. For each x with 0 <= x < n, let children(x) = { y | 0 <= y < n and parent[y] = x }, and let D(x) be the byte string obtained by concatenating D(y) for all y in children(x) in increasing numerical order and then appending the one-byte string s[x]. Then for every i with 0 <= i < n, r[i] = true if and only if D(i) is a palindrome, meaning that for every k with 0 <= k < len(D(i)), D(i)[k] = D(i)[len(D(i)) - 1 - k].
preconditions: n = len(parent) = len(s); 1 <= n <= 100000; parent[0] = -1; for every i with 1 <= i < n, 0 <= parent[i] < n; parent represents a valid tree rooted at node 0 (the directed graph with edges parent[i] -> i for 1 <= i < n has no cycles and every node reaches 0 by repeatedly following parent); for every i with 0 <= i < n, 97 <= s[i] <= 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < n, if r[i] = true then the first character of D(i) equals the last character of D(i). The last character of D(i) is s[i]. The first character is s[f(i)], where f(i) is defined recursively by f(i)=i if i has no children, and by f(i)=f(c) for the smallest child c of i otherwise. Thus r[i] = true implies s[f(i)] = s[i].
